question: Does verify.ps1 leave its temporary directory behind because MSBuild node reuse keeps dotnet.exe alive past the run, and does disabling node reuse fix it without changing checksums?

priorIncident.source: evidence/302-concurrent-full-runs.json (measured on PR #305, Issue #302), cited verbatim in Issue #306's own body
priorIncident.attribution: That PR's own writeup attributed it to 'several long-lived dotnet.exe MSBuild/Roslyn node-reuse worker processes ... holding a handle open', without naming a PID or confirming the mechanism against a live process. This Issue's brief asks for that confirmation before trusting the fix.

mechanism.method: Reproduced verify.ps1's own 'build' stage in isolation (dotnet restore of the solution, dotnet restore --locked-mode of the domain MCP test project, dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore), under the same DOTNET_CLI_HOME/TEMP/TMP environment verify.ps1 itself sets, then snapshotted dotnet.exe/VBCSCompiler.exe/MSBuild.exe processes before and after.
mechanism.result: 7 new dotnet.exe processes with command line '"C:\Program Files\dotnet\dotnet.exe" "C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk\8.0.423\MSBuild.dll" /nologo /nodemode:1 /nodeReuse:true /low:false' (PIDs 144688, 78008, 97660, 94468, 97696, 82992, 92352), plus one 'dotnet.exe exec ...VBCSCompiler.dll -pipename:...' (PID 136732, the shared Roslyn compiler server) - all still running when the script's own cleanup ran, and none of them spawned by anything other than this one restore+build.

stillAliveLater.result: All 8 PIDs still alive ~19 minutes after they were spawned, well past when a full verify.ps1 run's own cleanup would have run. PID 136732 (VBCSCompiler) has System.Text.Json.SourceGeneration.dll loaded as a shadow-copied analyzer module - the exact file evidence/302-concurrent-full-runs.json named as the lock that blocked cleanup - directly confirming which process class the earlier incident's 'dotnet.exe node-reuse worker' attribution meant.
stillAliveLater.caveat: That specific module's shadow-copy path was 'C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\VBCSCompiler\AnalyzerAssemblyLoader\...' - the machine's own TEMP, not this run's own owned temporary root - so this particular file is not itself what verify.ps1's cleanup deletes. It is evidence that this class of process (node-reuse dotnet.exe, VBCSCompiler) is real, spawned by this repository's own build, and outlives the run by a wide margin; the concurrent-run reproduction below is what shows the same class of process touching a run's own owned directory.

concurrentRunLeftover.method: Mirrored evidence/302-concurrent-full-runs.json's own method: two `verify.ps1 -Stage build` runs launched together, neither passing -TemporaryRoot, from two worktrees on unfixed scripts/verify.ps1 (git-stashed the fix in the claimed worktree; a throwaway sibling worktree _wt-306-repro-b at commit a44e14d for the other, removed after use).
concurrentRunLeftover.commandA: cd C:/gamedev/_wt-306 && powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify.ps1 -Stage build -GodotPath "C:/gamedev/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64_console.exe"
concurrentRunLeftover.commandB: cd C:/gamedev/_wt-306-repro-b && powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify.ps1 -Stage build -GodotPath "C:/gamedev/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64_console.exe"
concurrentRunLeftover.result: Both runs reported status ok with no temporary_cleanup warning line. Run A's own directory (C:\gamedev\df-verify-225c76ce) nonetheless still existed after the run finished, containing an empty 'NuGetScratch\lock' subdirectory (evidence/306-concurrent-a-leftover-listing.txt) created at the same second (14:38:05) as six fresh '/nodeReuse:true' dotnet.exe MSBuild workers were spawned for that same run (visible at 14:38:18 in the machine's process list, captured before this leftover was cleaned up). Run B's directory (df-verify-fb7349db) was fully gone, no leftover.
concurrentRunLeftover.interpretation: A different shape of the same defect from evidence/302's explicit warning: here Remove-Item's recursive delete completed and returned success with nothing to warn about, but a directory of the same name was recreated microseconds later - consistent with a NuGet operation still finishing on a node-reuse-kept-alive background process whose own TEMP was baked in as this now-deleted path at spawn time. No warning is emitted for this shape at all, which is worse than the shape Issue #89's best-effort design was built for: the run reports full success and still leaves a directory behind.
concurrentRunLeftover.cleanup: The leftover C:\gamedev\df-verify-225c76ce was removed by this session (Remove-Item -Recurse -Force, unattributed to any other agent - it was this repro's own directory, named with this repro's own randomly generated suffix).
concurrentRunLeftover.recreatedAfterDeletion: It came back. Checked again ~11 minutes later, after the fixed full run below had finished: C:\gamedev\df-verify-225c76ce\NuGetScratch\lock existed again, timestamped 14:49:31 - after the manual deletion, and after the six /nodeReuse:true workers from run A (spawned 14:38:18) were still confirmed alive. This machine also had other agents' worktrees (_wt-296, _wt-312, _wt-248, _wt-313-coord) running their own dotnet activity throughout this window, and node reuse is a machine-wide pool keyed by SDK version and architecture, not by caller - any of them requesting a reusable node without disabling reuse could have been handed one of run A's own still-alive nodes, which still carries run A's now-deleted directory as its own environment's TEMP from when it was spawned. This is the residual risk this fix does not retroactively clean up: MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1 stops verify.ps1 from creating new leaked nodes going forward, but nodes already leaked before every concurrent user of this machine sets it can keep resurrecting an already-deleted run's directory for as long as they stay alive and someone reuses them. Removed a second time before finishing this task; not attributable to any run this fix could have prevented, since it predates the fix being applied anywhere on this machine.

fixApplied.change: scripts/verify.ps1 sets $env:MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE = "1" alongside its other run-scoped dotnet environment variables (DOTNET_CLI_HOME, DOTNET_NOLOGO, ...), so every dotnet child process this script starts - restore, build, test, the domain MCP launcher and verification script - inherits it.

confirmationTheEnvVarReachesMSBuild.method: Captured the machine's live process list while today's post-fix full verify.ps1 run was in its build stage.
confirmationTheEnvVarReachesMSBuild.result: PID 52232, command line '"C:\Program Files\dotnet\dotnet.exe" "C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk\8.0.423\MSBuild.dll" /nologo /nodemode:1 /nodeReuse:false /low:false' - MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1 is not just set in the environment, it visibly flips MSBuild's own node-launch flag from /nodeReuse:true to /nodeReuse:false.

confirmationNoSurvivors.method: Snapshotted dotnet.exe processes whose command line matches 'nodeReuse' or 'VBCSCompiler' immediately before and 2 seconds after running `verify.ps1 -Stage build` with the fix applied.
confirmationNoSurvivors.result: NEW_NODEREUSE_OR_VBCS_SURVIVORS=0 - no new node-reuse or compiler-server process outlived this invocation.

buildStageTiming.note: Rule 8: numbers below are two samples each way on a machine shared with other agents' concurrent dotnet/test activity (visible in the process listings taken during these runs - other worktrees' restores and test runs overlapped both arms). The variance across samples of the same configuration (before: 10.5s and 15.5s; after: 7.3s and 18.9s) is larger than any plausible effect of node reuse alone on a solution this size, so no reliable direction could be measured here - reported as-is rather than picking the pair that tells a cleaner story.

before.command: git stash; powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify.ps1 -Stage build -GodotPath ... -TemporaryRoot C:\gamedev\df-verify-306-before-stage
git stash; powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify.ps1 -Stage build -GodotPath ... -TemporaryRoot C:\gamedev\df-verify-306-before-stage-2

buildStageTiming.theoreticalCost: Node reuse's benefit is amortised across many separate dotnet/MSBuild invocations sharing warm worker processes; disabling it means every restore/build in every future verify.ps1 invocation pays full node-startup cost instead of sometimes reusing an already-running one. That cost exists by MSBuild's own design even though it was not distinguishable from this machine's background noise in the samples above.

fullRunAfterFix.result: status ok, all 9 stages executed, no temporary_cleanup warning anywhere in the output.
fullRunAfterFix.temporaryRoot: C:\gamedev\df-verify-999ec814 - confirmed absent immediately after the run (Test-Path -> false / 'No such file or directory').
fullRunAfterFix.noNewNodeReuseSurvivors: Process list taken right after this run completed shows every dotnet.exe matching '/nodeReuse:true' or 'VBCSCompiler' by CreationDate predates this run's own start (14:22, 14:36, 14:38 - all from the earlier 'before' experiments above); none were created during this run's own scripts/build/tests/mcp/godot/ui/screenshots stages.
